Salisbury Steak

ByJaclyn Shimmel Published10/13/202610/13/2026
Listen to audio version of this article

This easy Salisbury steak recipe is classic comfort food made with simple ingredients. Tender ground beef patties seasoned with onion, Worcestershire, and a little ketchup simmer in a savory brown gravy, all in one skillet.

The gravy starts with a couple of brown gravy packets, then gets beef broth and the drippings left from browning the patties. The packets keep it no-fuss, and the drippings give it more flavor than the packet alone.

If you love easy ground beef dinners as much as I do, add my Slow Cooker Salisbury Steaks, Lipton Soup Mix Meatloaf, and Copycat Cracker Barrel Meatloaf to your list too. The slow cooker version is a good pick when you want the crockpot to do the work.

Why You’ll Love This Recipe

  • Ready in about 30 minutes – Ten minutes of prep, then dinner cooks in one skillet.
  • One pan – The patties and gravy cook in the same skillet, so the drippings go straight into the gravy and cleanup is easy.
  • Shortcut gravy – Brown gravy packets do the heavy lifting, while beef broth and the pan drippings give it more depth.
  • Plenty of gravy – About 2 cups, enough for the patties and a big pile of mashed potatoes.

Ingredients

This section includes ingredient notes and substitution options. Get all measurements, ingredients, and instructions in the printable recipe card at the end of this post.

  • Egg, breadcrumbs, and finely diced onion – These hold the patties together and keep them tender. Use regular breadcrumbs, not panko. Regular breadcrumbs absorb more moisture and hold the patties together better.
  • Ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, salt, and pepper – For seasoning the ground beef patties.
  • Ground beef – Use 85/15 or 80/20 lean ground beef so that the patties have some fat for flavor and moisture.
  • Olive oil and sliced onion – The onion cooks around the patties while they brown, and it flavors the drippings that go into the gravy.
  • Brown gravy mix – Two packets. I use McCormick’s lower-sodium brown gravy mix.
  • Beef broth, water, and ketchup – Combine with the gravy mix to make a pourable gravy. Low-sodium broth helps prevent the gravy from getting too salty.
  • Salt – Optional. Taste the gravy before adding.

How to Make Salisbury Steak

This section shows you how to make the recipe with step-by-step photos and instructions. For the full printable recipe, see the recipe card below. 

Step 1: In a medium bowl, mix together the egg, breadcrumbs, diced onion, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, salt, pepper, and garlic powder.

Step 2: Add the ground beef and mix gently with your hands until combined. Divide it into 4 equal balls and let them rest for 5 to 10 minutes.

Step 3: Add the oil and sliced onion to a large skillet over medium-high heat.

Step 4: Once the oil is hot, shape each ball into an oblong patty about 1 inch thick. Set the patties in the skillet, moving the onion slices around them.

Step 5: Sear for about 4 minutes per side, until a nice brown crust forms. They won’t be cooked through yet. Move them to a plate.

Step 6: Turn the heat down to low. Add the gravy mix, beef broth, water, ketchup, and salt if using. Stir until the gravy mix dissolves, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom of the pan as you go.

Step 7: Turn the heat up to medium-high and bring the gravy to a simmer.

Step 8: Once it reaches a simmer, lower the heat to medium-low and return the patties to the skillet. Cover and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, flipping once, until the center of each patty reaches 160°F. Stir the gravy as needed, and keep a close eye on the pan toward the end so the patties don’t stick.

Step 9: Serve warm over mashed potatoes with plenty of gravy spooned on top.

Serving Suggestions

Mashed potatoes are a must with all that gravy. My Old-Fashioned Mashed Potatoes and Red Skin Mashed Potatoes are both great here. Egg noodles or rice also work if you’d rather skip the potatoes.

For a vegetable, Southern Green Beans round out the plate. If you want more ideas, I have a list of 16 Easy Potato Side Dishes too.

Storage and Freezing

Refrigerator

Store leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days. Save every bit of the gravy for reheating.

Freezer

Let the patties and gravy cool, then freeze them together in an airtight container for up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge before reheating.

Reheating

Warm in a covered skillet over medium-low heat or in the microwave until heated through. The gravy thickens as it sits, so stir in a teaspoon or two of water to loosen it if needed.

Tips for the Best Salisbury Steak

  • Let the meat rest. The 5 to 10 minute rest gives the breadcrumbs time to soak up the egg and seasonings.
  • Keep the patties an even thickness. About 1 inch all the way across means the edges don’t dry out before the centers are done.
  • Onions around, not under. Patties sitting on onion slices won’t brown well, and that brown crust is what flavors the gravy.
  • Don’t cook them through on the first sear. They finish in the gravy, so pulling them early keeps them tender.

Additions and Variations

  • Extra-tender patties – Add 2 tablespoons of half-and-half to the meat mixture. The patties come out very tender, so handle them gently in the skillet so they don’t fall apart.
  • Onion or mushroom gravy – If your skillet has room, cook extra sliced onion or mushrooms alongside the patties while they brown. If it’s crowded, sauté them on their own after the patties come out, then make the gravy in the same pan.

Salisbury Steak FAQ

What is Salisbury steak?

Salisbury steak is a seasoned ground beef patty, usually mixed with breadcrumbs, egg, and onion, then simmered in brown gravy. It’s a classic American comfort food dinner.

What is Salisbury steak named after?

It’s named after Dr. James Salisbury, an American doctor in the 1800s who promoted eating patties made from chopped beef.

Is hamburger steak the same as Salisbury steak?

They’re close, but not the same. Both are ground beef patties served with brown gravy. The difference is in the meat mixture. Hamburger steak is usually seasoned with little more than salt and pepper, while Salisbury steak mixes in egg and breadcrumbs to bind the patties, plus seasonings like Worcestershire and ketchup.

Easy Salisbury Steak

Author: Jaclyn
Prep: 10 minutes mins
Cook: 20 minutes mins
Total: 30 minutes mins
This easy Salisbury steak recipe has tender ground beef patties simmered in a savory brown gravy made with gravy packets, beef broth, and pan drippings. Everything cooks in one skillet in about 30 minutes.
Servings: 4
Print
Pin
SaveSaved!
Rate

Ingredients

For the patties:

  • 1 large egg
  • ¼ cup breadcrumbs, not panko
  • 3 tablespoons finely diced onion
  • 1 tablespoon ketchup
  • 2 teaspoons Worcestershire sauce
  • ¾ teaspoon salt
  • ¼ teaspoon pepper
  • ¼ teaspoon garlic powder
  • 1 pound ground beef, I use 85/15
  • 1 tablespoon olive oil
  • ¼ onion, sliced

For the gravy:

  • 2 (0.87-ounce) packets low-sodium brown gravy mix
  • 2 cups low-sodium beef broth
  • ¼ cup water
  • 2 tablespoons ketchup
  • salt, optional, to taste

Instructions

Make the patties:

  • In a medium bowl, mix the egg, breadcrumbs, diced onion, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, salt, pepper, and garlic powder.
    1 large egg, ¼ cup breadcrumbs, 3 tablespoons finely diced onion, 1 tablespoon ketchup, 2 teaspoons Worcestershire sauce, ¾ teaspoon salt, ¼ teaspoon pepper, ¼ teaspoon garlic powder
  • Add the ground beef and mix gently. Divide into 4 even balls and let rest for 5 to 10 minutes.
    1 pound ground beef
  • Heat the olive oil and sliced onion in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
    1 tablespoon olive oil, ¼ onion
  • Once the oil is hot, shape each ball into an oval patty about 1 inch thick, as even as possible. Add to the skillet with the onion slices around the patties, not under them.
  • Cook about 4 minutes per side, until a nice brown crust forms. They do not need to be cooked through. Move to a plate.

Make the gravy:

  • Turn the heat to low. Add the gravy mix, beef broth, water, and ketchup. Stir until dissolved, scraping up the drippings from the bottom of the pan.
    2 (0.87-ounce) packets low-sodium brown gravy mix, 2 cups low-sodium beef broth, ¼ cup water, 2 tablespoons ketchup
  • Raise the heat to medium-high and bring the gravy to a simmer.
  • Reduce the heat to medium-low and return the patties to the skillet. Cover and cook 10 to 12 minutes, flipping once, until the patties reach 160°F inside. Stir the gravy as needed and watch closely toward the end so the patties do not stick.
  • Taste the gravy and add salt if needed. Serve warm over mashed potatoes with plenty of gravy.
    salt

Notes

Ground beef: Use 80/20 or 85/15. Leaner beef makes drier patties.
Storage: Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 4 days.
Freezing: Freeze the patties and gravy together in an airtight container for up to 2 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge before reheating.
Reheating: The gravy thickens in the fridge. Stir in a teaspoon or two of water while reheating.
